issues.title: Every shipped sniff source fails `phpcs --standard=rules.xml` — dogfood the ruleset against its own code
issues.body:
Follow-up from Holmes's review of #64 (PR #228), where the "Operators: Passive" sniff's own source was noted as not passing the master ruleset. On investigation this is **systemic**, not specific to that sniff — **none** of the shipped sniff sources pass `vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=rules.xml` against themselves.

**Observation:** the package lints consumer code to a standard its own source does not meet. Verified error counts (this review, against `rules.xml`):

- [ ] `CleanCode/Sniffs/CleanCode/OneConditionPerLineSniff.php` — 16 errors
- [ ] `CleanCode/Sniffs/WhiteSpace/BlankLinesSniff.php` — 10 errors
- [ ] `CleanCode/Sniffs/CleanCode/OneThoughtPerLineSniff.php` — 9 errors
- [ ] `CleanCode/Sniffs/CleanCode/DisallowDebugFunctionsSniff.php` — 3 errors
- [ ] `CleanCode/Sniffs/Classes/DisallowStaticMembersSniff.php` — 2 errors
- [ ] `CleanCode/Sniffs/WhiteSpace/PassiveOperatorSpacingSniff.php` — 5 errors (new in #64; already conforms to the sibling pattern, no worse)
- [ ] **Decision needed on the `Sniff::process(File $phpcsFile, $stackPtr)` interface method.** Two of the passive sniff's five errors are missing native type hints on `process()`; all six sniffs leave `$stackPtr` untyped by uniform convention, because narrowing it to `int` breaks contravariance with the PHPCS `Sniff` interface. Either exclude the interface-method signature from `SlevomatCodingStandard.TypeHints.ParameterTypeHint` for sniff sources, or document the exception — pick one and apply it uniformly.
- [ ] Add a CI step that dogfoods the sniff sources against `rules.xml` (today CI only runs the ruleset against `tests/bootstrap.php`), so new sniffs can't silently regress the source-cleanliness bar.

**Why it's worth doing:** a linter whose own source violates its rules is a credibility gap, and — because repo conventions win, so agents copy the established pattern — every new sniff replicates the debt (as #64 did, deliberately, to stay consistent with its siblings). Fixing it needs a decision (the interface type-hint question) plus a per-file sweep, so it is a schedulable chunk with a testable "done," not a 10-minute cleanup.

**Tracked under:** systemic-debt

Non-blocking, and unrelated to the coherent unit #64 delivers (the passive-operator standard itself works and is fully tested) — this is repo-wide code quality, tracked as one umbrella for the class rather than folded into #64. Raised (and offered up) by Watson during the round-2 fixes; opening it here so that work is captured and Watson does **not** chase it inside #64's scope.

<!-- followup-from: PR#228 -->

<!-- expand-from: PR#287 -->

<!-- expand-from: PR#244 -->
**Additional case for this issue**, surfaced reviewing PR #244 (issue #79, `IfStatementAssignment`):

**Observation:** PR #244 wires `Generic.CodeAnalysis.AssignmentInCondition` into `rules.xml`. Running just that sniff (plus the PR's own `CleanCode.Conditionals.DisallowListAssignmentInCondition`) against this repo's own `CleanCode/` source turns up 4 pre-existing self-triggering sites that the PR did not touch:

- `CleanCode/Sniffs/Arrays/ConvertToCollectionSniff.php:262`
- `CleanCode/Sniffs/Files/NoProceduralCodeSniff.php:132`
- `CleanCode/Sniffs/Controllers/NoCustomActionsSniff.php:133`

All four are the same idiom: `while (($x = f()) !== false)` (assign-and-test), which is exactly what the new rule reports as a smell.

**Why it's this issue's, not #79's:** PR #244 actually did fix one instance of this exact class — `CleanCode/Sniffs/Controllers/ManualModelResolutionSniff.php`'s `conditionPointer()` hoisted its own match-subject assignment out of the condition specifically to avoid self-triggering the new rule — but that was reactive spot-fixing, not a sweep, and 4 siblings remain. A full sweep belongs to this issue's "dogfood the ruleset against its own code" scope, not to each individual rule-adding PR.

**Repro:** `vendor/bin/phpcs --standard=rules.xml --sniffs=Generic.CodeAnalysis.AssignmentInCondition,CleanCode.Conditionals.DisallowListAssignmentInCondition CleanCode/ --ignore="*/fixtures/*"` → 4 errors, none in files PR #244 touched.

**Tracked under:** systemic-debt

Lestrade: fold this into the acceptance criteria (one checkbox per site, or a general "assign-and-test idiom" sweep line item, whichever this issue's existing AC shape prefers).

<!-- watson-blocked: scope -->
## Blocked on scope — the AC cannot be one PR

I measured the tree before starting. The AC's final item asks for a full `phpcs --standard=rules.xml` run over `CleanCode/` at 0 errors. That run currently reports:

```
1813 ERRORS AND 1565 WARNINGS IN 73 FILES
phpcbf can fix 485 of 3378 violations automatically
```

Measured on `main` at `50c488d`, ignoring `*/fixtures/*`. The issue body was written against 6 files and 45 errors. The tree grew to 68 sniff files since then. The AC is stale by two orders of magnitude.

### Where the errors come from

Errors only, warnings excluded, because only errors gate the AC:

| Rule | Errors |
|---|---|
| `CleanCode.Arrays.ArrayAccessors` (element + property) | 1022 |
| `CleanCode.Conditionals.OneConditionPerLine` | 224 |
| `SlevomatCodingStandard.TypeHints.*` | 155 |
| `CleanCode.CleanCode.OneThoughtPerLine` | 62 |
| `CleanCode.Strings.MultilineStrings` | 54 |
| `CleanCode.Metrics.MethodNestingLevel` | 53 |
| 20 further rules | ~243 |

`CleanCode.Conditionals.AvoidConditionals` produces 960 more findings. Those are warnings, so they do not gate the AC. Holmes's comments on this issue treat them as blocking. They are not.

### The one-PR problem

`ArrayAccessors` alone is 56 percent of all errors, across 41 of 68 sniffs. Three facts make it expensive:

1. The sanctioned fix is `data_get()`. That is a Laravel helper. `rules.xml:537-539` states this package deliberately does not ship it.
2. The `File` API is not a complete substitute. It exposes `findNext`, `getCondition`, and `getTokensAsString`. It exposes no accessor for `scope_closer`, `parenthesis_opener`, `level`, or `nested_parenthesis`. 41 sniffs read those through the token array.
3. A workaround does exist. I verified it live: the sniff exempts `$this`-rooted access, so `$this->tokens[$ptr]['scope_closer']` passes while the identical local `$tokens[$ptr]['scope_closer']` fails.

Fact 3 is the problem, not the solution. Hoisting the token array onto a sniff property puts per-file mutable state on an object PHP_CodeSniffer reuses across files and across fixer loops. That is the stale-cache shape this repo already bounced twice, on PR #264 and PR #300. Applying it to 941 read sites in 41 files, each needing proof that detection behavior did not change, is not a formatting sweep.

The remaining ~790 errors are not formatting either. `MethodNestingLevel`, `CyclomaticComplexity`, `ExcessiveClassComplexity`, and `AvoidDuplicateCodeBlocks` need sniff logic restructured.

The CI gate the AC asks for is coupled to all of this. A gate that runs `rules.xml` over `CleanCode/` fails on push until every file is clean. I cannot land a green gate without the whole sweep.

### Three stale paths in the AC

These three do not exist. The files moved:

- `CleanCode/Sniffs/CleanCode/OneConditionPerLineSniff.php` is now `Sniffs/Conditionals/`
- `CleanCode/Sniffs/CleanCode/OneThoughtPerLineSniff.php`
- `CleanCode/Sniffs/CleanCode/DisallowDebugFunctionsSniff.php` is now `Sniffs/Debug/`

### One AC item is already answered

The AC asks for a uniform decision on the `Sniff::process(File $phpcsFile, $stackPtr)` type hint. The repo already made it. `ManualModelResolutionSniff.php:130-137` carries a docblock plus `// phpcs:ignore SlevomatCodingStandard.TypeHints.ParameterTypeHint.MissingNativeTypeHint`. PR #168 established that pattern, because narrowing the inherited parameter to `int` is a fatal error. Whoever sharpens this AC should record that as settled convention, not as an open question.

## Options

1. **Narrow the gate to an applicable subset.** Add a dogfood ruleset that excludes the Laravel-application rules for `CleanCode/**` — `ArrayAccessors` and `ConvertToCollection` — and require 0 errors under the rest. Ship the CI gate in one PR.
   Pros: deliverable now, gate is real, stops new debt immediately.
   Cons: the two largest rules stay undogfooded. The "linter meets its own bar" claim gets an asterisk.

2. **Keep 0 errors under the full ruleset, and slice by directory.** Split into per-directory child issues under this umbrella, `Sniffs/Conditionals/`, `Sniffs/Strings/`, and so on. Land the CI gate last, once the tree is clean.
   Pros: honors the AC's intent with no carve-out.
   Cons: 10 or more PRs. The gate protects nothing until the final one merges. Needs the token-access decision answered first.

3. **Ratchet.** Land the CI gate now against an allowlist seeded with the files that already pass. Add files to the allowlist as later PRs clean them.
   Pros: one PR now, no carve-out, and the bar only moves one way.
   Cons: an allowlist is a debt register that needs maintaining. New sniffs are gated, old ones are not, until each is fixed.

**Recommendation: 1.** It is the only option that makes the CI gate real in one PR, and the gate is what stops the debt growing. `ArrayAccessors` and `ConvertToCollection` name helpers this package refuses to depend on, so exempting the sniff tree from them states an existing decision rather than making a new one.

Option 1 still needs a call I will not make alone: whether `$this->tokens` hoisting is the package's sanctioned token-access style. That decision binds every future sniff. Route it to Mike if you pick option 2 or 3, where it is load-bearing.

No branch and no PR exist. I measured before creating either, so there is nothing to clean up. Send this back once the AC is sharpened, and I will implement against it.

<!-- lestrade-escalated-scope -->
@mikebronner — sending this back up instead of re-sharpening the AC. Watson's kickback isn't "the wording is unclear," it's "the coherent unit is two orders of magnitude bigger than the AC assumed."

Watson measured `main` at `50c488d`: 1813 errors / 1565 warnings across 73 files, not the 6 files / 45 errors the AC was written against. 56% of the errors (1022) are one rule — `ArrayAccessors` — hitting 41 of 68 sniffs, and the sanctioned fix (`data_get()`) is a Laravel helper this package deliberately doesn't ship (`rules.xml:537-539`). The workaround that does exist — hoisting the token array onto `$this` — puts per-file mutable state on a PHPCS object that gets reused across files and fixer loops, the same stale-cache shape that already bounced PR #264 and PR #300. That's not a formatting sweep across 941 read sites in 41 files; it's a design decision.

I'm not slicing this myself — right-sizing is yours. Watson framed three paths; I've reviewed them and they hold up:

1. **Narrow the gate.** Dogfood ruleset excludes `ArrayAccessors`/`ConvertToCollection` (the Laravel-app rules) for `CleanCode/**`, require 0 errors on everything else, ship the CI gate in this one PR. *Pros:* real gate, ships now, stops new debt today. *Cons:* the two biggest rules stay undogfooded — "the linter meets its own bar" ships with an asterisk.
2. **Full ruleset, sliced by directory.** Child issues per sub-namespace (`Sniffs/Conditionals/`, `Sniffs/Strings/`, etc.), CI gate lands last once the whole tree is clean. *Pros:* honors the AC's original "0 errors, full standard" intent, no carve-out. *Cons:* 10+ PRs, the gate protects nothing until the last one lands, and it still needs the token-access decision settled first.
3. **Ratchet.** Land the gate now against an allowlist seeded with files that already pass; each future PR adds its file once clean. *Pros:* one PR, no carve-out, bar only moves one direction. *Cons:* the allowlist is itself a debt register somebody has to maintain, and old sniffs stay ungated indefinitely.

**Recommendation: option 1.** It's the only path that makes the CI gate real in one PR — and the gate, not the sweep, is what stops the bleeding. Excluding `ArrayAccessors`/`ConvertToCollection` from the sniff-source dogfood isn't a new carve-out, it restates a decision this package already made (no Laravel deps in the ruleset itself).

One decision is load-bearing across all three options and isn't mine to make: is `$this->tokens`-style hoisting the package's sanctioned token-access convention for future sniffs, or off the table? Options 2 and 3 can't proceed without it; option 1 sidesteps it entirely, which is the other reason it's the cleanest cut.

Also: one AC item is already resolved, not open. The `process()` type-hint question was settled by PR #168 — `// phpcs:ignore SlevomatCodingStandard.TypeHints.ParameterTypeHint` plus a docblock (see `ManualModelResolutionSniff.php:130-137`). Whoever rewrites the AC should record that as convention, not reopen it as a decision.

Leaving the AC as originally written — it also has three stale paths (`OneConditionPerLineSniff`/`OneThoughtPerLineSniff`/`DisallowDebugFunctionsSniff` moved out of `Sniffs/CleanCode/` since this was opened) — for whoever re-authors this at the right size.

Sweep note: 3 `<!-- expand-from -->` comments (PR#287, PR#168, PR#244) are sitting on this issue unfolded into AC. Leaving them — this item is `Escalated` pending Mike's right-sizing call, and the prior `lestrade-escalated-scope` comment deliberately left the AC as originally written for whoever re-authors at the right size. Folding more cases in now would rewrite the contract mid-decision. Next sweep after this re-lands at the right scope should fold them.

issues.title: Replace wall-clock-vs-threshold assertions across 7 sibling test files — same flakiness hazard as #321
issues.body:
Follow-up from Holmes's review of #321 (PR #351).

**Observation:** #321/PR #351 replaced two `hrtime()`-ratio assertions in `tests/Standards/UnusedFormalParameterTest.php` with deterministic cache-rebuild/cache-hit counters, because a wall-clock comparison against a small baseline is inherently noisy on a shared CI runner (confirmed: the original assertion failed twice and passed on a third run with no code change). A repo-wide grep for the same shape (`hrtime()` elapsed time compared against a fixed-value or ratio threshold via `toBeLessThan`/`toBeGreaterThan`) turns up **7 more test files** carrying the identical hazard pattern:

- [ ] `tests/Standards/ArrayAccessorsTest.php` (`:371,408,414,456` — multiple `toBeLessThan(3.0|…)` and a growth-ratio `toBeLessThan(2.5, …)`)
- [ ] `tests/Standards/CombinableConditionsTest.php` (`:343` — `toBeLessThan(3.0)`)
- [ ] `tests/Standards/DisallowChainedPropertyFetchTest.php` (`:646` — `toBeLessThan(3.0, …)`)
- [ ] `tests/Standards/LogicalGroupingsTest.php` (`:318,452` — ratio thresholds `toBeLessThan($skipped * 4)` / `* 2`)
- [ ] `tests/Standards/MappingArrayCandidateTest.php` (`:234` — `toBeLessThan(2.0)`)
- [ ] `tests/Standards/NPathComplexityTest.php` (`:631` — `toBeLessThan(2.0)`)
- [ ] `tests/Standards/MultiLineStatementIndentTest.php` (`:509,549,594` — multiple `toBeLessThan(3.0|1.0, …)`)

**Why it's worth doing:** each of these is a live recurrence of the exact same hazard #321 fixed — a shared CI runner's ordinary jitter can push an elapsed-time measurement across a fixed threshold with no code change, causing a spurious failure. #321/PR #351 explicitly scoped itself to `UnusedFormalParameterTest.php` only (a different unit of work per its own AC's "no other file" clause), and PR #351's description flags this exact list as out-of-scope rather than silently leaving it undiscovered. Each site will need its own sniff instrumented with deterministic counters (or another non-wall-clock discriminator), the same way #321 did — not a single mechanical fix, hence tracked as one class rather than filed as 7 separate near-duplicate issues.

**Tracked under:** systemic-debt

Non-blocking — none of these have been observed to flake in CI yet (unlike #321's case, which had two observed CI failures before being fixed), so this is a preventive sweep rather than an active-incident fix. A single PR (or a few, split by natural sniff boundaries) can close individual checkboxes here as they're addressed; check the box and leave a comment noting the fix when a file is done, rather than closing this issue until all 7 are cleared.

<!-- followup-from: PR#351 -->

comments.body:
<!-- acceptance-criteria -->

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Delivered as a single PR covering all 9 files below** (the 7 originally scoped plus 2 more of the identical hazard shape folded in during retriage — see the widening comment on this issue). Do not decompose into multiple issues or multiple PRs — per @mikebronner's explicit override on this issue (2026-08-27). The PR description enumerates, per file, the exact line number(s) of the `hrtime()`-vs-threshold assertion(s) removed (matching this checklist's own line citations) and pastes the output of `grep -n "toBeLessThan\|toBeGreaterThan"` across all 9 files confirming no `hrtime()`/`microtime()`-derived value remains compared against a fixed value or ratio anywhere in the diff — appearing in the diff is not, by itself, evidence a file's hazard was actually removed.
- [ ] **Unblocked:** #321/PR #351 (the reference instrumentation this issue extends) merged to `main` on 2026-08-19 at commit `3637e8114ab4ec1374c24d0cd760ea6bdcace426`. Every "same way as #351" reference below is verified against that merged commit on `main`, not the PR's original description.
- [ ] For each of the 9 files below, every assertion comparing an `hrtime()`-derived elapsed-time measurement directly against a fixed-value or ratio threshold (`toBeLessThan`/`toBeGreaterThan`) is replaced with an assertion on a deterministic, non-timing discriminator **causally coupled to the specific optimization/guard being protected** — not a proxy that merely correlates with it (raw input size, total tokens in the file, or a counter on the instrumentation call itself rather than on the guarded branch does not satisfy this). `hrtime()`/`microtime()` may remain for diagnostic/logging output only, never as a pass/fail input. Because `tests/Helpers.php`'s `buildRuleset()` memoizes the built ruleset+sniff instance in a process-wide static cache (including a `'*master*'` key when called with no sniff-code argument, shared across every test in the same PHP process since `composer test` runs Pest single-process/non-parallel), every counter-reading assertion is sourced from a sniff instance obtained via a single-sniff-code-scoped `buildRuleset([CODE])`/`analyzeWithSniffs([CODE], ...)` call — never the no-args master-ruleset path — and read as a delta captured immediately before/after the one `process()` call under test, never a raw cumulative total carried across loop iterations, doubling sizes, or other tests sharing a memoized instance. **Every file's fix must include a documented, reproducible mutation check**: the PR description names the specific optimization/guard being reverted (by function/branch, confirmable via `git blame` that the branch predates this PR), includes the actual diff hunk of that one-line/one-branch reversion, and pastes the resulting `composer test` failure output showing the new counter-based assertion reddens — a prose-or-table before/after-count summary in the docblock is required *in addition to*, not instead of, that reproducible evidence. The same mutation run also records whether the file's existing non-timing (violation-count/line/column) assertions still pass or fail, so the counter is shown to track behavior the surrounding test already cares about, not an assertion invented solely to satisfy this checkbox.
- [ ] `tests/Standards/ArrayAccessorsTest.php`: `it('decides enclosing constructs in linear time')` (:371), `it('decides a staggered staircase within the cost of parsing it')` (:408 and :414, two assertions in that one test), and `it('grows linearly across each doubling of a staggered staircase')` (:456) are fixed together in one commit, since :408/:414/:456 all consume the same shared closure `$arrayAccessorsStaircaseTiming` (lines 77-124) — that closure is redesigned once, not patched independently per call site, to return counter deltas from the enclosing-construct map instead of `[$errors, $parsed, $sniffed]` elapsed seconds. The counter must be captured as a delta immediately around each size's `process()` call inside the doubling loop (matching #351's UFP discipline), not read as a running total carried across sizes or across other `ArrayAccessorsTest.php` tests that share the closure's memoized instance. The :456 growth-ratio assertion specifically needs a counter that is not itself (nor trivially derived from) the input size — it must measure steps/lookups actually performed per staircase level — and the mutation check for this test must show the *ratio bound itself* reddens (not merely that the counter is non-zero) when the closure's optimization is reverted to quadratic; the replacement bound must be freshly derived and documented (a numeric analogue of the old 2.5x), not dropped.
- [ ] `tests/Standards/CombinableConditionsTest.php`: the elapsed-time assertion in `it('stays linear on long runs and deep nesting')` (:343) is replaced with a deterministic counter on the sniff's scan/token-visit path, mutation-verified per the general item above.
- [ ] `tests/Standards/DisallowChainedPropertyFetchTest.php`: the elapsed-time assertion in `it('decides a chain in time linear in its length')` (:646, both `plain` and `interleaved` shapes) is replaced with a counter on the "already-visited" record the sniff uses to bound the chain walk, mutation-verified per the general item above. The counter's reset-coupling to the existing "already-visited" record clear is *proven*, not assumed: this file's mutation check specifically removes only the counter's reset (leaving the visited-record clear intact) and confirms `it('keeps no record across files')` (:664) reddens as a result — that test merely continuing to pass under the full fix is not sufficient evidence the two resets are coupled. The PR description states explicitly whether the counter itself resets per file (like the record it replaces) or accumulates and is read as a delta, consistent with how :664's three staged runs (`failing.php` → `passing.php` → `failing.php`) exercise it.
- [ ] `tests/Standards/LogicalGroupingsTest.php`: the two ratio assertions (`toBeLessThan($skipped * 4)` at :318, `toBeLessThan($skipped * 2)` at :452) are replaced with a discriminator that preserves the original ×4/×2 bounds as exact step-count comparisons, mutation-verified per the general item above. The chosen counter must be scoped to conditions/tokens actually visited during the sniff's grouping-walk attempt, **including its early-exit path** — not file-wide token/condition counts or any counter decoupled from the grouping walk's own control flow, since a decoupled counter could read non-zero on the "skipped" control fixture (`nested-calls.php`, deliberately built to trigger zero grouping-walk work) without ever tracking real grouping work. A counter that legitimately reads 0 on `$skipped` makes `$grouped < 0` unsatisfiable and is not an acceptable replacement either way.
- [ ] `tests/Standards/MappingArrayCandidateTest.php`: the elapsed-time assertion in `it('stays linear on deeply nested chains')` (:234) is replaced with a deterministic counter distinguishing the reordered (body-token-first) walk from the quadratic body-materialization walk it replaced, mutation-verified per the general item above.
- [ ] `tests/Standards/NPathComplexityTest.php`: the elapsed-time assertion in `it('stays linear on a long chain of ternaries')` (:631) is replaced with a counter on the memoized ternary-chain scan (hit vs. re-scan count), mutation-verified per the general item above.
- [ ] `tests/Standards/MultiLineStatementIndentTest.php`: the three elapsed-time assertions (:509 long-comment read, :549 comment-anchor read, :594 opener-line anchor read) are each replaced with their own independently-asserted counter on `mapLines()`'s carried state (e.g. `mapLines.longComment.rescans`, `mapLines.commentAnchor.rescans`, `mapLines.openerAnchor.rescans`) — not one pooled/shared counter across the three tests. Independence is *proven*, not just named: each of the three mutation checks also confirms the *other two* counters are unaffected by that specific reversion (e.g. reverting the long-comment guard reddens only `mapLines.longComment.rescans`, leaving the other two unchanged).

issues.title: ComponentMarkupSniff: opensOnAComponent()/areAdjacent() silently misjudge on TEMPLATE_WRAPPER's preg_replace() failure (same defect class as #318/#334)
issues.body:
Follow-up from Holmes's review of #334 (PR #355).

**Observation:** `opensOnAComponent()` (`CleanCode/Sniffs/Livewire/ComponentMarkupSniff.php:415-420`) and `areAdjacent()` (`:603-609`) both call `preg_replace(self::TEMPLATE_WRAPPER, '', $gap)` and coerce the result with `(string) preg_replace(...)`, then check `trim(...) === ''`. `TEMPLATE_WRAPPER` (`:117`) reuses the identical `(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|[^<>"'])*` attribute-run alternation that `TEMPLATE_TAG` is documented (by PR #355 itself) to fail on via `PREG_JIT_STACKLIMIT_ERROR` (~8,190 chars, JIT on) / `PREG_RECURSION_LIMIT_ERROR` (~99,995 chars, JIT off). Neither call site checks `preg_replace()`'s return for `null` before casting — a failed match is silently coerced to `''`, and `trim('') === ''` reads as "nothing between them," the same unchecked-return-value defect class #318 and #334 both fixed elsewhere in this file.

Adversarially verified during PR #355's review (full red-team/blue-team/auditor panel — all three independently reproduced against the live tree, not a hunch):
- **Attacker:** reproduced end-to-end through the project's own test harness. A root `<div wire:model="x">` followed by a `<template>` tag carrying an ~8,200-character throwaway attribute value, then a `<livewire:card>` tag — a genuinely non-compliant root that should fire `RootElementAttributes` — produces **zero** errors/warnings when the decoy `<template>` is present (control run, same markup minus the decoy, correctly fires `RootElementAttributes`).
- **Defender:** confirmed no length cap, no prior successful-match gate, and no bounds check anywhere upstream of either `preg_replace()` call — unlike `componentTags()`/`templateTags()` (this PR's own subject) and `isComponentView()` (#318/PR #333), none of which have this gap anymore.
- **Auditor:** independently reproduced via PHP reflection against the actual production class, confirmed `opensOnAComponent()` returns `true` (bypassing `RootElementAttributes`) at exactly the documented 8,190-character JIT-on threshold. Confirmed the defect is real and reachable, but refuted it as a *blocker* for PR #355 specifically — it's outside that PR's AC, explicitly disclosed in the PR description under "Scope boundaries," and matches this repo's own established precedent (#333 disclosing #334's own subject matter the same way one PR earlier).

**Location:** `CleanCode/Sniffs/Livewire/ComponentMarkupSniff.php:117` (`TEMPLATE_WRAPPER`), `:415-420` (`opensOnAComponent()`), `:603-609` (`areAdjacent()`)

**Why it's worth doing:** `opensOnAComponent()`'s failure mode is a detection bypass (a non-compliant root silently escapes `RootElementAttributes`), reachable by anyone authoring the Blade file the sniff lints, with no privileged access required. `areAdjacent()`'s failure mode is the opposite direction — spurious `AdjacentComponentNotWrapped`/`TemplateKeyMismatch` false positives. Bounded cost either way (~milliseconds, JIT-dependent), consistent with #334's own severity disposition — doesn't clear DoS/blocker severity on its own, same as #334 didn't before it was fixed.

**Tracked under:** latent-hazard

Non-blocking, but material — an observation *unrelated* to the coherent unit PR #355 delivers (that unit is scoped, by #334's own AC, to `preg_match_all()` in `componentTags()`/`templateTags()` only). Not part of #334's acceptance criteria. Surfaced and adversarially verified during review of PR #355.

<!-- followup-from: PR#355 -->

comments.body:
<!-- acceptance-criteria -->

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `opensOnAComponent()` (`CleanCode/Sniffs/Livewire/ComponentMarkupSniff.php:415-420`): on a `TEMPLATE_WRAPPER` read failure — `preg_replace(self::TEMPLATE_WRAPPER, '', $gap)` returning `null` — the method returns `false` immediately, without ever passing the failed result through `trim()`/`(string)` cast or substituting `''` (or any other string) for the `null`. So `RootElementAttributes` is **not** suppressed on a genuinely non-compliant root — closing the detection-bypass direction the issue describes.
- [ ] `areAdjacent()` (`CleanCode/Sniffs/Livewire/ComponentMarkupSniff.php:603-609`): on the same `TEMPLATE_WRAPPER` read failure, the method returns `false` immediately, with the identical no-substitution constraint above. So `AdjacentComponentNotWrapped`/`TemplateKeyMismatch` are **not** spuriously reported on siblings whose gap could not be read — closing the false-positive direction the issue describes.
- [ ] Both methods' docblocks independently restate (not cross-reference each other) the failure mode at the same rigor as `templateTags()`'s docblock (`:816-836`): the specific PCRE error constant(s), `TEMPLATE_WRAPPER`'s *own* measured JIT-on/JIT-off character thresholds — re-measured directly against `TEMPLATE_WRAPPER`, not assumed identical to `TEMPLATE_TAG`'s (it adds the `<\/?` closing-tag alternative, so the threshold isn't guaranteed to match — the way `componentTags()`'s docblock re-measured `COMPONENT_TAG`'s thresholds rather than reusing `ELEMENT_TAG`'s) — and which false-negative/false-positive direction the guard closes for that specific call site.
- [ ] A new fixture reproduces the issue's own "Attacker" repro for `opensOnAComponent()`: a root element carrying a disallowed Livewire/Blade/Alpine attribute, followed by a `<template>` tag whose attribute run is sized the way `unreadable-template-tags.php` sizes its own (comfortably past *both* the ~99,995-char JIT-off and ~8,190-char JIT-on thresholds — e.g. ~600,000 characters — so the failure reproduces regardless of the running PHP's `pcre.jit` setting), followed by a `<livewire:…>` tag. A test proves `RootElementAttributes` is now reported against the fixed code (silently suppressed pre-fix), asserting the complete violation map (e.g. `allViolationSourcesByLine()`) and empty warnings — not a loose containment check.
- [ ] A new fixture reproduces `areAdjacent()`'s false-positive direction: two sibling components separated by a gap that drives the same oversized `TEMPLATE_WRAPPER` read failure (sized per the bullet above) but is not actually empty/whitespace-only. A test proves `AdjacentComponentNotWrapped`/`TemplateKeyMismatch` is **not** reported against the fixed code, asserting the complete violation map and empty warnings.
- [ ] Both new fixtures include a control case, mirroring the existing `unreadable-*-tags` tests' own control assertions: the same markup with the oversized run shrunk/removed so the `TEMPLATE_WRAPPER` read succeeds, proving the sniff's answer flips to the correct result once the gap is actually readable — ruling out a fixture that would produce the same verdict regardless of whether the regex fails.
- [ ] Both new test cases include a reflection-based precondition, adapted from (not copy-pasted from) `tests/Standards/ComponentMarkupTest.php`'s existing `unreadable-*-tags` tests: because `opensOnAComponent()`/`areAdjacent()` call `preg_replace()` rather than `preg_match_all()`, the precondition calls `preg_replace(self::TEMPLATE_WRAPPER, '', $gap)` directly (pattern read via `ReflectionClassConstant`), asserts the result `=== null` (not `=== false`, which is `preg_match_all()`'s failure signal, not `preg_replace()`'s), and reads `preg_last_error()` immediately after — asserted conditionally on `ini_get('pcre.jit')` (`PREG_JIT_STACKLIMIT_ERROR` when on, `PREG_RECURSION_LIMIT_ERROR` when off), never a hard-coded constant. The precondition call itself is unsuppressed (no `@`).
- [ ] Both new test cases assert no PHP warning or error escapes the sniff run (`phpunit.xml.dist`'s `failOnWarning`), independent of the unsuppressed reflection-precondition call above.
- [ ] Existing fixtures under `tests/fixtures/ComponentMarkupSniff/` continue to pass unchanged, and the fix is verified — not just fixture-compatible — to detect failure by checking `preg_replace()`'s actual return value, ruling out a size-based heuristic (e.g. an early `strlen($gap) > N` bailout) that happens to pass the same fixtures without implementing the checked-return-value fix.
- [ ] Scope stays confined to `opensOnAComponent()` and `areAdjacent()` — the two call sites named in the issue title. No change to `componentTags()`, `templateTags()`, `isComponentView()`, or `attributeNames()`.

<!-- lestrade-ac-verified -->
Tightened the acceptance criteria after adversarial review (4-lens fan-out: malicious-compliance, testability, completeness, edge-case):

- **JIT-sizing (3 lenses independently flagged this):** the two new fixtures must be sized the way `unreadable-template-tags.php` already is — comfortably past *both* the ~99,995-char JIT-off and ~8,190-char JIT-on thresholds (~600,000 chars), not just the issue's own ~8,200-char repro size, so the failure reproduces regardless of the running PHP's `pcre.jit` setting. The reflection precondition now asserts `preg_last_error()` conditionally on `ini_get('pcre.jit')` instead of a hard-coded constant.
- **Wrong failure signal (malicious-compliance lens):** `opensOnAComponent()`/`areAdjacent()` call `preg_replace()`, which fails via a `null` return — not `preg_match_all()`'s `false`. A naive copy of the existing `unreadable-*-tags` test pattern would assert the wrong thing entirely; the AC now spells out `preg_replace()` + `=== null` explicitly.
- **Null-swallowing loophole (malicious-compliance lens):** the original wording ("checks the return value for null") was satisfiable by checking for null and substituting `''` right back in, reproducing the exact bug. Now requires `false` returned immediately, with no substitution.
- **Control case (edge-case lens):** both new fixtures now require a shrink/remove control proving the sniff's answer flips back to correct once the gap is actually readable — matching the existing `unreadable-*-tags` tests' own structure.
- **Self-contained docblocks + re-measured thresholds (malicious-compliance + edge-case lenses):** docblocks must restate the failure mode independently (no cross-referencing the sibling method) and re-measure `TEMPLATE_WRAPPER`'s own thresholds rather than assuming `TEMPLATE_TAG`'s transfer unchanged — mirroring how `componentTags()`'s docblock re-measured `COMPONENT_TAG` rather than reusing `ELEMENT_TAG`'s numbers.
- **Precise violation assertions (malicious-compliance lens):** both new tests must assert the complete violation map + empty warnings, not a loose containment check.

One testability-lens finding was discarded: it claimed `templateTags()` has no failure-mode docblock and never checks its return value, and that only one `unreadable-*-tags` fixture exists. I re-fetched the file directly and both claims are false — `templateTags()` (lines 816-870) documents the constants/thresholds and does check `$matched === false`, and there are three `unreadable-*-tags` fixtures/tests (element, component, template), not one. Citation stands as originally written.

issues.title: main is red: ConvertToCollection reviewed-site census lost 4 line pins to the #288 merge (recurrence of #356)
issues.body:
`main` fails CI at HEAD. The failure blocks every open PR. No branch can reach a green gate while it inherits this.

This is the second time this ledger has broken this way. #356 was the first.

## The failing test

`tests/Standards/ConvertToCollectionTest.php` — `it('reports only the reviewed sites across the package source')`. It compares the sniff's live findings against `CONVERT_TO_COLLECTION_REVIEWED_SITES`, the hand-maintained ledger issue #286 left behind.

| Commit | PR | Run | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `5b61167` | #300 | [33098979271](https://github.com/mike-bronner/phpcs-rules/actions/runs/33098979271) | green |
| `6496e5e` | #288 | [33099028811](https://github.com/mike-bronner/phpcs-rules/actions/runs/33099028811) | **red** |

Four pins drift, across two files. Every column is unchanged. Every other ledger key matches exactly.

```
'tests/Helpers.php'  expected 641 / 810 / 1594   found 686 / 855 / 1673
'tests/Sniffs.php'   expected 236                found 239
```

## The diagnosis

The merge of #288 moved the pins **backwards**, to numbers that were never correct on `main`.

| File | `main` at `5b61167` | `main` at `6496e5e` | True |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tests/Helpers.php` | 657, 826, 1644 | 641, 810, 1594 | 686, 855, 1673 |
| `tests/Sniffs.php` | 238 | 236 | 239 |

`git diff 5b61167 6496e5e -- tests/Standards/ConvertToCollectionTest.php` shows the merge rewriting `657 → 641`, `826 → 810`, `1644 → 1594` and `238 → 236`. Those lowered numbers are the #193 feature branch's own copy of the ledger, stale since it forked. Git took the branch side of the conflict instead of the `main` side.

The correct numbers are arithmetic. #288 added 29 lines to `tests/Helpers.php` and 1 line to `tests/Sniffs.php`, all above the pinned calls:

```
657 + 29 = 686      826 + 29 = 855      1644 + 29 = 1673      238 + 1 = 239
```

Each sum is the observed value.

## No new call site entered the sweep

The four calls are the same four calls. Their source lines are byte-identical before and after the merge:

| Was | Is | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `Helpers.php:657` | `686` | `[$stdout, $stderr, $status] = runOutsidePackage(implode(' ', array_map('escapeshellarg', $arguments)));` |
| `Helpers.php:826` | `855` | `$counts[$line] = array_sum(array_map('count', $columns));` |
| `Helpers.php:1644` | `1673` | `implode(' ', array_map('escapeshellarg', [PHP_BINARY, '-d', 'error_reporting=-1', '-r', $script]))` |
| `Sniffs.php:238` | `239` | `$custom = array_filter($swept, static fn (string $code): bool => str_starts_with($code, 'CleanCode.'));` |

The per-file counts are also unchanged: three sites for `tests/Helpers.php`, one for `tests/Sniffs.php`. A human reviewed all four already. Only the line numbers moved. The repair blesses no new call, so it does not weaken the guard.

## The fix

```php
'tests/Helpers.php' => [
    ['line' => 686, 'column' => 66],
    ['line' => 855, 'column' => 36],
    ['line' => 1673, 'column' => 22],
],
```

```php
'tests/Sniffs.php' => [
    ['line' => 239, 'column' => 15],
],
```

**Verified.** Apply those four numbers to a clean tree and the full suite is green: `1 skipped, 2600 passed (7531 assertions)`, zero failures. Without them the same tree reports `1 failed, 1 skipped, 2599 passed`, which is what CI reports.

## Why this is its own issue

I found this while implementing #366 on PR #368. That PR touches `ComponentMarkupSniff.php` and its tests. It touches no `ConvertToCollection` file and neither of the two drifted files. Its own acceptance criteria confine it to two methods.

A clean `origin/main` worktree reproduces the failure with none of PR #368's commits present. The failure output is byte-identical with and without that branch.

The repair belongs to `main`, not to an unrelated Livewire PR. #356 set that precedent for the same ledger.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CONVERT_TO_COLLECTION_REVIEWED_SITES` records `tests/Helpers.php` as exactly three sites, at lines 686, 855 and 1673, with columns 66, 36 and 22 unchanged.
- [ ] The same constant records `tests/Sniffs.php` as exactly one site, at line 239, column 15.
- [ ] Each of those keys appears exactly once in the source. A later duplicate key that overrides an earlier one at evaluation time does not satisfy this.
- [ ] Every other ledger key is unchanged, and nothing else in `ConvertToCollectionTest.php` changes — including `$convertToCollectionSweptFiles`.
- [ ] `composer test` passes on `main` with zero failures.
- [ ] The ledger has now broken this way twice, in #356 and here, both times from a textual merge of concurrent edits to a line-number list. #356's last criterion asked whether a guard is worth adding and the answer was deferred. Record a decision this time: add the guard, or write down why the recurrence is acceptable.

A decision that only proposes a smarter ledger-correctness check without addressing that the red run itself never blocked the merge does not satisfy this — it must explicitly say whether required-status-check protection is being enabled for `main`'s test job, or why a CI-detects-but-doesn't-block posture is acceptable after two recurrences.
  - If a mechanical check is added, it runs automatically (CI or a pre-commit/composer script — not a documentation checklist a human is trusted to run) and verifies each ledger tuple resolves to a call of its recorded kind at its recorded position.
  - If no guard is added, the paragraph ends with an explicit sentence of the form "No guard is being added because ___" — a paragraph that only describes the two prior failures without stating and justifying that decision does not satisfy this.

Tightened the acceptance criteria after adversarial review (four blind lenses):

- **Duplicate-key evasion by evaluated key, not spelling**: "appears exactly once" was checkable by grepping one literal quoting — a differently-quoted or concatenated duplicate key evaluates to the same string but would dodge a textual check. Now requires verification by evaluated key count.
- **Order-sensitivity**: the test's `->toBe()` comparison is strict and order-sensitive; the three `Helpers.php` tuples now must land in the stated order, not just as a set.
- **Source-file padding closed off**: nothing previously stopped satisfying the tuple checkboxes by padding `tests/Helpers.php`/`tests/Sniffs.php` themselves to relocate the calls onto the demanded numbers, instead of correcting the ledger to the calls' real (unmoved) position. Added an explicit byte-identical-to-pre-fix-main requirement for both source files.
- **Dropped an unfalsifiable checkbox**: the draft asked for evidence against "the issue's diagnosis table" naming `array_map()`/`array_filter()` — that table doesn't exist in the issue body in that form, and the byte-identical-source-file check above proves the same thing (unmoved calls) more rigorously. Removed rather than patched.
- **Transcript authenticity**: a restated summary line was indistinguishable from a fabricated one. Now requires the raw command output, not just the summary.
- **Guard decision, enforcement not just detection**: verified directly against the repo — `main` has no required-status-check branch protection, and the reviewed-sites test was red on both #356 and #369, yet both merged anyway. The recurring failure isn't "the check didn't notice," it's "nothing required the check to pass." The guard criterion now must address branch-protection/enforcement explicitly, not just ledger-data-shape correctness, and closes off "not boilerplate" as a subjective bar by requiring both issues named by number, both mechanisms named specifically, and an explicit decision sentence if no guard is added.

## The repair in this issue already landed. Only the guard decision is left, and it needs your call.

### What I verified on `main` at `e65cdfc`

You fixed the four pins yourself in `448c87c` ("test(arrays): re-point four sweep sites main moved"), merged through #367 at 12:00:20 PDT. This issue was filed at 12:32 PDT, 32 minutes later. The diagnosis in the body is correct but it is no longer current.

| Acceptance criterion | State on `main` |
|---|---|
| `tests/Helpers.php` → `686/66`, `855/36`, `1673/22`, in that order | Already correct |
| `tests/Sniffs.php` → `239/15` | Already correct |
| Each key written exactly once, by evaluated key count | 71 written keys, 71 evaluated keys, no duplicates |
| `composer test` full and unfiltered | `1 skipped, 2606 passed (7521 assertions)`, zero failures |
| CI on `main` | Run at `e65cdfc` completed `success` |

I checked the key count by evaluating every written key expression with `token_get_all()`, not by grepping a literal spelling. A differently quoted or concatenated duplicate would have shown as a written count above the evaluated count. It did not.

So a data-repair PR would be an empty diff. Criterion 6 is the only work left.

### Why I stopped

Criterion 6 requires the PR to state one of two things: that required-status-check protection **is being enabled** for `main`'s test job, or **why** a CI-detects-but-does-not-block posture is acceptable after two recurrences.

I can state neither honestly.

I cannot enable branch protection. It is a repository administration setting, and it changes how you merge your own repository from now on. That is your decision, not mine.

I will not write the second statement either. I confirmed the enforcement gap directly: `GET /branches/main/protection` returns 404 "Branch not protected", and `GET /rulesets` returns `[]`. The reviewed-sites test was red for both #356 and #369. Both merged. The `main` push run at `6496e5e` was red and stayed red for two and a half hours. Detection worked twice. Nothing ever required it to pass. A paragraph arguing that this posture is acceptable would contradict the evidence in this issue.

### The options

**Option A — Enable required-status-check protection on `main`, and add the mechanical ledger guard.**
The guard checks that each ledger tuple still resolves to a call of its recorded kind at its recorded position. Protection makes a red check block the merge.
Cost: you enable the protection setting; I write the guard. You can no longer merge a red PR without an override.
Against it: the guard largely duplicates a check that already exists. The reviewed-sites test compares live sniff findings against the ledger. That is the same question, and it caught both recurrences.

**Option B — Enable required-status-check protection on `main`. Add no new guard. (My recommendation.)**
Both failures share one mechanism at the merge: a textual merge of a line-number list took the stale branch side. Neither failure was a detection failure. A second checker would report what the first checker already reported, and it would not stop the bad merge resolution either — it would only report it, from a check that still does not block.
Cost: you enable one setting. I write the decision paragraph and the PR carries no code change.
Against it: nothing stops the drift from being introduced, only from being merged.

**Option C — Add neither. Record why the current posture is acceptable.**
Both recurrences were caught the same day and repaired within hours, and you are the only maintainer.
Against it: this is the posture that has now failed twice. I do not recommend it, and I would not be able to write its justification in good faith.

### What I need

Pick A, B, or C. For A or B, also confirm you will enable the protection, because I cannot.

The branch `chore/369-main-is-red-converttocollection-reviewed-site-cens` and draft PR #370 stay open. I will implement your choice on that same branch when this comes back to me.

issues.title: Wire CleanCode.Arrays.DuplicatedArrayKey against the package's own test source
issues.body:
Follow-up from Holmes's review of #369 (PR #370).

**Observation:** The repo already ships `CleanCode.Arrays.DuplicatedArrayKey`, a sniff purpose-built to catch a duplicate top-level array key silently overriding an earlier one at evaluation time. It is never run against the package's own test source (`tests/Standards/*.php`) — including `tests/Standards/ConvertToCollectionTest.php`, home of the `CONVERT_TO_COLLECTION_REVIEWED_SITES` ledger that broke twice (#356, #369).

**Location:** `tests/Standards/DuplicatedArrayKeyTest.php` (and `SniffContractTest.php` / `ShippedPackageSmokeTest.php`) — every call site that exercises this sniff points it only at `tests/fixtures/DuplicatedArrayKeySniff/*`. No test passes it `cleanCodeRoot() . '/tests/Standards/...'` or any other package-source path.

**Why it's worth doing:** It's a real, cheap, already-built guard sitting unused. To be precise about scope: it would **not** have caught either #356 (a 3-way merge that accumulated stale tuples inside one key's array *value* — confirmed against #356's own body and PR #360, which explicitly states "no second, later key overrides it") or #369 (a merge that reverted to a stale branch-side value) — neither was an actual duplicate-key defect. But it's a real hazard against a *different*, plausible failure in the same family: an actual duplicate top-level key appearing somewhere in test source. Wiring it in (one assertion pointing the existing sniff at `tests/Standards/`) costs little and closes a real gap.

**Tracked under:** latent-hazard

Non-blocking on PR #370 — unrelated to the coherent unit that PR delivers (recording the #356/#369 guard decision), not named by #369's acceptance criteria, and not caused by that PR's (empty) diff.
